title: The Crimson Bride
story: The hand beaded crimson silhouette built for a bride who refused the white reception convention.
Beulah designed the corset to read as red carpet from the front and as bridal from the side, so every photograph from every angle delivered the same headline.
Eight to twelve weeks. Three fittings. Hand bead motif unique to the bride.

title: The Coral Aso Ebi
story: Built in batches for whole families, modified per body so the set photographs as a family but reads as individuals.
Structured corset top, soft trumpet skirt with detachable train.
Six sets in four weeks if the deposit lands before the third week.

title: The Boardroom Navy
story: The two piece set Beulah designed for a CFO who needed one look to do a board meeting in the morning and an investor dinner that evening.
Cut sits clean over the hip without ever clinging. Reads as authority over a navy shell, soft power over silk.

title: Sunday Champagne
story: Champagne silk with a hand finished hem, oversized matching kimono.
Worn over the slip for brunch, over jeans for a flight, over linen for a meeting that pretends not to be one.

title: The Beaded Bride
story: Hand beaded across the bodice, French tulle from waist to floor.
Beulah personally pencils the bead pattern after the first consultation; no two layouts have ever been repeated.

title: The Sapphire Aso Ebi
story: Sapphire with gold thread detail; built for a sister-of-the-bride party of seven.
Bulk pricing for families of four or more.

title: The Signing Suit
story: Two piece in deep navy with hand bound buttonholes and a tapered ankle.
Designed for the contract signing, the press photo, and the dinner after.

title: Soft Life Sage
story: Sage silk slip on the bias, hand hem, oversized shawl collar kimono.
Two fittings, ten to fourteen days from confirmation.

title: The Reception Look
story: The second look for the bride who does not want to leave the dance floor.
Cocktail length, hand bead at the hem, removable cape detail.

title: The Family Aso Ebi
story: The set Beulah builds for mothers and aunties when they refuse to be styled like the bridesmaids.
Adjustable across body shapes; the silhouette holds.

title: The Executive Cream
story: Hand picked cream for boardroom lighting; the cut sits clean over the hip without ever clinging.
Worn over a navy shell or a silk camisole, two rooms, two outcomes.

title: The Velvet Hour
story: Crushed velvet midi with a soft drape neckline.
Designed for the dinner where you arrive last and the room turns.

title: The Ivory Bride
story: The civil ceremony piece for the bride who wants the gown without the train.
Hand draped, lined silk, cut to be photographed seated and standing.

title: The Burgundy Aso Ebi
story: Deep burgundy with a hand worked gold motif at the cuff.
The set most often worn to traditional engagements that turn into receptions.

title: The Power Two-Piece
story: Hand tailored two piece for the woman whose presence enters the room before her name.
Lined throughout, cut to sit clean across a four hour meeting.

title: The Linen Hour
story: Lagos linen, hand finished, cut for the heat without losing the line.
Worn unbelted to brunch; belted to a meeting; tied at the waist for everything else.

title: The Trad
story: The traditional engagement look for the bride who does not want to be wearing the same set as her cousin.
Made to commission; six to ten weeks from deposit.

title: The Rose Build
story: Dusty rose, lace bodice, soft chiffon skirt.
The piece for the brunch that becomes a launch announcement.
